A shelving system that reconfigures between three distinct states: upright bookcase, horizontal desk surface with integrated storage, and open shelving wall. The same set of panels, the same connectors, three completely different pieces of furniture. The project ran from system design through component engineering and into physical prototyping.

The system

Regal 3.0 is built from a standardised panel grid. Each panel carries the same slot and tab geometry on all four edges, so any panel can connect to any other in any orientation. The module dimensions were derived from an ergonomic analysis of reach zones: the tallest configuration puts its top shelf at the upper limit of comfortable standing reach; the lowest puts its working surface at seated desk height.

Two panel types: the primary body panel with integrated slot rails, and the narrower side panel that sets the depth. Every drawer, shelf, and partition is a combination of these two. No unique components except the locking bracket.

Body panel

The variants

Three configurations were developed and drawn to full dimensions, each verified against ergonomic reach data for both standing and seated postures.

Posizione A — Libreria

The upright bookcase. Panels stacked vertically with drawers in the lower section and open shelves above. Full height of 1499 mm keeps the top shelf within comfortable standing reach. Footprint stays narrow at 372 mm deep.

Footprint
1499 × 372 mm
Height
1317 mm

Posizione B — Tavolo + Mensola

The desk configuration. The same panels rotate 90 degrees: the body becomes the working surface, drawer units sit beneath, and a narrow shelf rises behind. Seated ergonomic analysis confirmed the surface sits at correct typing height. This is the configuration the D1 locking bracket was designed to stabilise.

Width
1190 mm
Desk height
471 mm
Shelf height
1317 mm

Posizione C — Parete

The full wall configuration. Panels arranged horizontally across a 1674 mm span with mixed drawer and open-shelf sections. The widest of the three variants, suited to a living room or studio as a room-defining element.

Width
1674 mm
Height
1499 mm

The locking component

Posizione B introduces a structural problem the slot-and-tab system alone cannot solve: when the main body tilts to become a desk surface, it needs a rigid bracket to hold the angle under load. The D1 component was designed specifically for this.

The D1 is a Y-shaped bracket that slides through the panel slot, rotates 90 degrees, and locks against the interior face. Two arms distribute the load across the panel thickness; the central stem acts as the pivot. No tools, no fasteners to install or remove.

Height
38.2 cm
Width
30.2 cm
Stem depth
26 cm
Material
PLA · 3D printed

From design to prototype

The D1 was taken through to a physical prototype via FDM 3D printing. Before printing, the component was analysed in slicer software to verify wall thickness, infill density, support requirements, and print orientation. The cross-section visualisation confirmed the curved arms would print cleanly without supports if oriented vertically.

Print time
12 min
Weight
3 g · 1.1 m filament
Layer height
0.2 mm
Wall lines
3 · 1.2 mm total
Slicer legend
Outer wall · Inner wall · Top/Bottom · Infill · Printed component. The colour-coded cross-section confirmed that the arm curvature would print without internal voids at the junction between stem and arms.

The process

The project ran across three deliverable steps: the functional component abaco and panel layout, the full technical drawing of the D1 locking bracket, and the slicer analysis and physical print. Each step fed directly into the next; the dimensions on the abaco set the slot tolerances the D1 technical drawing had to match, and the technical drawing set the geometry the slicer had to validate.

Course: Sustainable Advanced Design, Corso Interdisciplinare di Product Design. Supervised by Prof. Consuelo Nava with Arch. Domenico Lucanto and PhD St. Eliana Catalano.
